extraFacts.fact: Dinamic Oil GB in-line heavy-duty planetary gearbox: peak torque 281,000 to 3,620,000 Nm, 1 to 5 stages. GBA right-angle: 281,000 to 2,720,000 Nm, 3 to 6 stages. RE in-line: 1,780 to 198,000 Nm, 1 to 5 stages. RA right-angle: 1,780 to 198,000 Nm, 2 to 4 stages.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics listings for the Dinamic Oil planetary gearbox ranges

faqs.q: What is the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes used for?
faqs.a: The Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes are heavy-duty in-line planetary gearboxes for the largest drives. The range has 15 frame sizes, GB 12010 to 235000, with peak output torque (T2max) of 281,000 Nm to 3,620,000 Nm and ratios of 3.43:1 to 3,673.37:1 in 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 stages; typical uses are sugar-cane mills, shredders, steel-plant and mining machinery, thickeners and large winch and slewing drives.

faqs.q: How do I read a Dinamic Oil model number such as GB 12012?
faqs.a: The first part is the frame size and the last digit is the number of planetary stages: in the size table GB 12011 is the 1-stage model and GB 235005 the 5-stage model. An L suffix marks the light composition, available for some ratios; the table lists all 75 stage models.

faqs.q: Which frame sizes and torque ratings do the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes cover?
faqs.a: The Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes cover 15 frame sizes, GB 12010 to 235000, with peak output torque (T2max) of 281,000 Nm to 3,620,000 Nm by frame. The size table gives each stage model its ratio range, for example GB 12011 at 4.09 – 6.23 and GB 235005 at 891.47 – 2902.95. The ratio-by-ratio table of output speed, input power and torque at 750, 900, 1,450 and 2,900 rpm input is in Dinamic Oil's catalogue, and we send the page for the model you shortlist.

faqs.q: Is T2max the torque to select the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes on?
faqs.a: No. For the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes, T2max (281,000 Nm to 3,620,000 Nm) is the peak torque the gearbox may see occasionally. Select on the continuous output torque the application needs multiplied by its service factor, keep starting and braking peaks below the peak rating, and check thermal power and the radial and axial loads on the output shaft; [our guide to selecting a planetary gearbox](/blog/how-to-select-a-planetary-gearbox) walks through it.

faqs.q: What is the rated torque and what is it rated to for the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes?
faqs.a: Peak output torque is 281,000 Nm to 3,620,000 Nm by frame, and Dinamic Oil rates the range to ISO 6336 for the gears and ISO 281 for the bearings. Where the transmitted power exceeds the thermal power, as on continuous duty in a hot climate, Dinamic Oil supplies oil/water (URO/W) and oil/air (URO/A) cooling units that dissipate up to 50 kW.

faqs.q: What oil does the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes need and how is it supplied?
faqs.a: The Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes ship unpainted and without oil, so fill with an EP gear oil of ISO VG 220 to 320 before start-up. The first oil change is after 150 hours, then at the catalogue interval or at least every 2 years; [our guide to planetary gearbox oil in hot climates](/blog/planetary-gearbox-oil-in-hot-climates) covers hot-climate oil.

faqs.q: Do the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes carry a class approval?
faqs.a: The Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes listing gives a project or unit certificate on request (DNV, ABS, LR, BV) rather than a standing type approval. Tell us the class society and project on the enquiry and we ask Dinamic Oil for the certificate before you order.

faqs.q: Which motors, brakes and outputs fit the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes?
faqs.a: Inputs are a universal ST input for most hydraulic motors, SAE flanges for orbital and axial piston motors, electric-motor adapters and male input shafts. Brakes are negative multi-disc, spring applied and hydraulically released (F1, F2, F5, F6, F8, F9 and MD); related items are on the [gearbox and winch accessories](/c/gearbox-winch-accessories) and the [planetary gearboxes](/c/planetary-gearboxes).

faqs.q: How are the Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Planetary Gearboxes installed and run in hot weather?
faqs.a: Dinamic Oil rates its standard units for an ambient temperature up to +40 °C. Above that, or where the unit runs continuously in direct sun, tell us the actual operating temperature so the lubricant and duty can be checked. The GB mounts horizontally and vertically, which sets the fill, level and drain plugs, and [our guide to planetary gearbox oil in hot climates](/blog/planetary-gearbox-oil-in-hot-climates) gives the lubricant guidance.

faqs.q: How does the Dinamic Oil GB differ from the GBA planetary gearbox?
faqs.a: The GB is the in-line, heavy-duty range. The sibling [Dinamic Oil GBA Heavy-Duty Right-Angle Planetary Gearboxes — 281 kNm to 2.72 MNm](/p/dinamic-oil-gba-heavy-duty-right-angle-planetary-gearboxes) is the right-angle GBA, which adds a CC bevel input head so the motor sits at 90° to the output. Pick on the layout the machine allows and the torque and ratio you need; [our guide to selecting a planetary gearbox](/blog/how-to-select-a-planetary-gearbox) compares the ranges.
